days.name: Monday · Theory, Phenomenon & Hypothesis
days.lesson: Frame **Earth System Modeling** as a physical or operational problem. Weather and climate emerge from interacting atmosphere, ocean, land, ice, biosphere, and human systems across many scales.
days.lab: Build a coupled Earth-system diagram with energy, water, carbon, and momentum pathways.
worksheet: Describe the phenomenon without explanation first; separate observation from interpretation.
Identify dependent/independent or diagnostic variables. Primary evidence: time, location, units, quantitative observations, mapped fields and model output.

days.name: Tuesday · Quantitative Laboratory

worksheet: Create a labeled data table with units, time, location/source and precision.
Apply computational-model reasoning and sensitivity testing. Show the calculation or decision rule.
Create an appropriate graph, profile, map, vector diagram or distribution.
Interpret the result in physical meteorological terms.

days.name: Wednesday · Data & Model Analysis
days.lesson: Use models as testable representations rather than pictures. Develop or revise a model explaining earth system modeling.
days.lab: Build, run or critique a physical, mathematical, conceptual or computational model related to earth system modeling.
worksheet: Use at least four terms accurately: atmosphere, Earth system, computation, evidence, uncertainty.
State governing relationships or causal links represented by the model.
Compare model output with at least one observation or expected physical constraint.
State one assumption, one limitation and one likely source of model error.

days.name: Thursday · Operational Analysis & Research
days.lesson: Apply the week's science to a real or archived atmospheric case using **Solanar Platform** plus an appropriate primary/official source.
days.lab: Use Solanar Platform to investigate a case. Archive location, valid time, product/source, variables and screenshots/notes as permitted.
worksheet: Classify each source as observation, official warning, forecast, numerical model, derived guidance, research/background or news.

State confidence and what new evidence could change your conclusion.

days.name: Friday · Forecast Briefing, Defense & Mastery

days.lab: Deliver a 3–5 minute forecast/science briefing or a one-page technical memorandum. Defend one key decision under questioning.
worksheet: CLAIM / FORECAST: state the conclusion precisely.
